# Independent audit of outer-contact perspective localization

Source: outer-contact-cap-selectors-and-perspective-localization-rate-geometry.md.



1. A hyperplane properly crossing a full-dimensional convex D intersects
   its boundary in an H_(d-1)-null set. Its section is full-dimensional
   within the hyperplane, and a relative-interior section point cannot
   be an ambient boundary point: any supporting normal there would have
   to be perpendicular to the section plane, contradicting proper
   crossing. Hence the intersection is contained in the relative
   boundary of the section. This proves that actual supporting
   allocations disappear on the outer contacts for arbitrary D,
   without strict convexity.

2. The gap g_n is affine, nonnegative on the entire actual body, and
   continuous in n. Nonnegative normal multiples of exp(-t g_n) belong
   to the actual convex physical cone. They are uniformly bounded on
   the boundary, so dominated convergence restricts the unchanged
   separator to the outer-contact graph. No arbitrary face-subset
   localization follows.

3. For nonnegative finite convex phi, the perspective
   ell phi((x-y)/ell) is convex on ell>0. The compact body has a
   neighborhood with a positive ell floor. Local Lipschitz continuity
   there bounds all supporting-affine coefficients on a slightly
   larger compact neighborhood. Their supremum is a globally finite
   convex function agreeing with the perspective on the body.
   For polyhedral phi the perspective is already a finite maximum of
   affine functions. Thus the positive-part field

       [ell phi((x-y)/ell)-t g_n]_+

   is a legitimate actual field and decreases on the body to
   ell phi((x-y)/ell) times the contact indicator. The exact facet
   weight after rescaling is ell^d, not ell^(d-1).

4. The projective energy first-moment equation makes the actual image
   xi -> xi/(1+a_D·xi) centered. Its cone boundary measure pulls back to
   h_D(n)/(1+a_D·xi)^d times dS_D. A through-zero cap has cone mass
   equal to d times its projective image volume. Every buffered cap
   contains the parallel through-zero cap, so the ordinary sharp
   Gamma_d theorem supplies the displayed cone credit. It is not
   necessary or correct to identify a shifted cap's cone mass with
   its full truncated volume.

5. Strict convexity is needed only to make the exposed point a
   function of the normal, so the same W is constant across the
   conditional contact fiber. The actual own source contributes a
   positive full copy of the surface-area measure. The conditional
   inequality therefore yields the stated pointwise bound and the
   restricted numerical conclusion.

The exact H response permits the sharper form

    beta+(d+2)Delta/(2dM)>=Gamma_d,

because all own-energy, own-volume and covariance terms in Xi are
nonnegative. This is the constant B_star recorded in
one-face-outer-envelope-cap-propagation-and-strict-convex-payment-optimal-midpoint.md.

No uniform-face centroid, lower-dimensional cap payment, or replacement
of the actual nonsmooth conditional contact density is inferred.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
